session_summary: CLAUDE.md population and codebase analysis. Dispatched config-editor (2m46s) to replace all placeholder values with real project data. Dispatched code-analyst (8m34s) for full 95-script analysis producing .voltron/analyses/2026-04-30-codebase-overview.md. Both completed successfully. Stringer baseline deferred -- stringer CLI not installed. Beads initialized with --server flag due to Windows CGO limitation.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Pre-computed line-number anchors in the task description enabled precise edits in a single pass. Agent completed in under 3 minutes with zero errors. The beads integration section was preserved perfectly.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Nothing significant -- the agent performed exactly as expected for a surgical edit task.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Produced a thorough 383-line analysis report with all 95 scripts categorized, 18 tech debt items with file references, and detailed documentation of 5 key systems. The handoff JSON was well-structured.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Agent took 8+ minutes (mostly API response time for the first call). The initial prompt response took over 4 minutes -- this is an API latency issue, not a template issue. The agent template instructs it to dispatch sub-agents but for a Unity project with no routes/DB/linting, most Inspect-layer agents are irrelevant. The DO NOT dispatch instruction in my task override was necessary.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: Add a Unity-specific recipe to the code-analyst template: for Unity projects, skip route-lister, schema-inspector, api-shape-probe, bundle-sizer, lint-reader, type-error-reader. Instead use direct file reading for script inventory, grep for patterns, and git log for recent changes.

overall_notes: Beads init on Windows requires --server flag (not --mode server) due to CGO requirement for embedded Dolt. The go-stringer Alexandria guide refers to golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stringer which is a different tool from the codebase analysis stringer (github.com/davetashner/stringer). Pre-computing line-number anchors before dispatching file-edit agents is critical -- the config-editor finished in 2m46s vs an estimated 15+ turns without anchors. Both agents ran in parallel successfully with the image build only needed for the first container.
